title: India
intro: Welcome to this lecture on the geography of India.

beats.say: India lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere, at the heart of South Asia.
With an area of about 3.287 million square kilometres, it is the seventh largest country in the world.

do.label: 7th largest country · 2.4% of world land area

beats.say: The Tropic of Cancer divides the country almost in half, passing through eight states.
Politically, India is a union of 28 states and 8 union territories, with New Delhi as its capital.

chapters.title: Rivers
chapters.narration: Chapter two. The rivers of India.

beats.say: Himalayan rivers are fed by both rain and melting snow, so they flow all year round.

do.text: Himalayan: snow and rain fed, perennial

beats.say: The Ganga, flowing about 2,525 kilometres to the Bay of Bengal, is India's longest river.
Most peninsular rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal, each ending in a fertile delta.
In early June, the south-west monsoon bursts over Kerala, and then advances in two branches.
Between June and September it brings about three quarters of India's annual rainfall.

do.label: of annual rain falls June to September

recap: June to September · three quarters of the rain
